MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 27, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on March 27, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 22, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Goodell (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation: Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9; Name of case: Webster et al vs. City of Mission Viejo.

CS2. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  March 27, 2018
 CS3. Conference with Real Property Negotiators - Government Code Section 54956.8:
  Property: Mission Viejo Village Center: Agency Negotiator, City Manager,
  Community Development Director, City Attorney: Negotiating Parties; HWA DAH
  LLC, The Patio in Mission Viejo, Trojan Sports LLC, Jann Gath, La Paz Viejo
  Company LLC, OC Generations V Limited Partnerships, 413 Adams Street
  Associates, Russell E. Fluter, Thomas Family Partners-Mission Viejo, Todd I.
  Schiffman, and MV Village Properties LLC.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:08 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for items CS1 and CS2, the Council received information
and gave direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred. Item CS3 was continued due to lack
of time.

Mr. Curley announced that when the Council addresses item 18, he will be asking them to add an
item to the agenda and determine (1) that the matter arose subsequent to the posting of the agenda
and (2) that there is a need for the Council to take action prior to the next City Council Meeting. He
said he will ask the Council to consider whether or not they would like join the amicus to support
the federal government's action in regards to the state's sanctuary laws. He also noted that the city
has been sued, but not served, relating to the Council's action to look at alternative remedies in the
voting rights matter. The City Attorney stated that a judicial order was required and is a
collaborative and cooperative way to advance to the alternative remedies that the Council directed
staff to look into. Mr. Curley said that he has spoken with attorney Kevin Shenkman who is in full
agreement and the two will be meeting soon to take the first steps towards understanding what the
alternative solutions are.

INVOCATION: Mayor Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Disneyland Resort’s Dreamers & Doers Program Recognition

  Mayor Sachs presented a Certificate of Recognition to Julia Ransom who was one of the
  top five Luminaries in the Dreamers & Doers Program. Julia organized and implemented
  a memorial 5K walk in Mission Viejo to raise money and awareness for mental health
  advocacy. Jen Deprez and Savannah Olson from Disneyland were also present to discuss
  the Dreamers & Doers Program and Julia’s efforts.

City Council Minutes  2  March 27, 2018
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Donna Marsh Peery, Immediate Past President of the California Association of Parks and Rec
Commissioners and Board Members: congratulated Mission Viejo Community Services
Commissioner Grant Voss for his award as “Commissioner of the Year” and former Community
Services Commissioner Ron Ruef for his “Lifetime Achievement” award. Mayor Sachs and the
entire City Council joined Ms. Marsh Peery to present a Certificate of Recognition to Grant Voss
on behalf of the city (Mr. Ruef was unable to attend the meeting but will receive his certificate at
another time).

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: said that there has been admission that the city is in violation of the
California Voting Rights Act, that Mayor Sachs’ March 10 newsletter was a joke and that attorney
Kevin Shenkman has filed a lawsuit and complaint against the city. She noted that she would hand
in documentation for the public record.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: stated that he is appalled at the level of purposeful misinformation during
public comments and the allegations asserted by one resident, in particular, who seems motivated
by a combination of sour grapes and political ambition. Mr. Rotcher said that no public speakers
have been prevented from speaking and the accusations that the Council’s actions on districting
have left the Council vulnerable are contradicted by the facts.

Ryan Farsai, M.V.: as one of the property owners of Anthony’s ARCO, he said he has been in
discussions with city staff regarding the sale of beer and wine at his store and restrictions that the
city has placed on his business. He stated that he seeks justice and hopes to come to a peaceful
solution.

The following expressed their discontent with the California Values Act (sanctuary state laws) and
illegal immigration: Ella Digirolamo, M.V.; Crystal Jade, Dana Point; Fred Macintosh, Downey.

The following expressed support for the California Values Act: Naui Huitzilopochtli, city of
residence unknown.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of March 13, 2018, as
  presented.
City Council Minutes  3  March 27, 2018
 2.  Check Register Dated March 2, 2018 in the Amount of $2,584,217.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated March 9, 2018 in the Amount of $811,802.17

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2018

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2018

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for January 2018

  Received and filed.

8.  Claim Against the City - Steinmeyer

  Rejected claim.

9.  Marguerite Parkway Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 17230)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Siemens Industry, Inc., in the
  amount of $599,597.00.

10.  Curb Address Number Painting, Southerly Section (CIP 18836)

  Awarded the painting contract for the subject project to Asphalt, Fabric and Engineering,
  Inc., in the amount of $34,500.

11.  Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting and Sealing Services

  Approved the Third Amendment to the existing contract with Bonanza Steam Cleaning,

City Council Minutes  4  March 27, 2018
 12.  Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2018-2019 Detailing City’s Proposed
  Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds.

  Adopted Resolution 18-12 Approving the City's Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year
  (FY) 2018-2019 Detailing the City’s Proposed use of Community Development Block
  Grant (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing Submission of one Plan to the U.S. Department of
  Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

13.  General Plan Progress Report for 2017

  Received and filed report.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

STAFF REPORTS

18.  Resolution Supporting the City of Los Alamitos Regarding Rejection of State Law-
  Sanctuary State

18B.  Amicus Brief that Supports the Federal Government’s Contention that Federal Law
  Preempts Contrary State Laws

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that at the last meeting, the Council Members were
  informed that all cities in California were contacted with the request to join an amicus brief
  in support of the federal government’s action against the state of California to overturn the
  three primary sanctuary state laws. The Council was receptive but wanted to see the amicus
  before taking any action. Mr. Curley noted that he just received the brief yesterday and the
  Council was provided a copy. He asked the Council Members to consider adding an item
  to the agenda and to find that the matter came to the city’s attention subsequent to the
  posting of the agenda and that there is a need to take immediate action.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  declare that the matter (item 18B) arose subsequent to the posting of the agenda, and (2)
  that there is a need for the Council to take action prior to the next City Council Meeting.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and discussed the option to support the
  City of Los Alamitos ordinance which asserts laws that are inconsistent with controlling
  federal laws should not apply to California cities.

  The following spoke in favor of the city's support of the Los Alamitos ordinance and in
  opposition to SB 54: John Willis, Ontario; Kim Sorgente, Huntington Beach; Arthur
  Schaper, Torrance; Nicole Soltero, Anaheim; Ashlee Soltero, Anaheim; Harim Uziel, Los
  Angeles; Vaughn Becht, Westminster; Kenny Strawn, M.V.; Cathy Skendrovich, M.V.;
City Council Minutes  5  March 27, 2018
   Jennifer Martinez, Garden Grove; Mike Metgetric, city of residence unknown; Vincent
  Foxx, city of residence unknown; Chanell Temple, city of residence unknown; Louie
  Reyes, M.V.; Ursula Yager, Irvine; Jesse S., city of residence unknown; Ian La Fontaine,
  La Palma; Beverly Welch, Costa Mesa; Kristi Maharvey, M.V.; Jessica Runfola, M.V.;
  Genevieve Peters, city of residence unknown; Benjamin Garcia, Irvine; Janine Ortell,
  M.V.; Gerald Thomas, Orange; Patrice Lynes, city of residence unknown; Eddie Baker,
  Juniper Hills; Stella May, city of residence unknown; Paul Jansen, Laguna Hills; Jessamine
  Augustine, M.V.; Cathy Schlicht, M.V.; Gerald Volomino, M.V.; Robin Huidstun, city of
  residence unknown; Raul Rodriques, city of residence unknown; Loree Masonis, city of
  residence unknown; Martin Kaezmarek, M.V.; Dura Young, Downey; and Steve Serra,
  M.V.

  The following made comments in support of SB 54 and the sanctuary state/city laws:
  Michael Rotcher, M.V.; Andrea Rangno, M.V.; and Tim Phan, Stanton.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 18-15 Supporting the City Council of the City of Los Alamitos in
  Adopting Ordinance 2018-03 Regarding Compliance with the United States Constitution;
  and (2) direct the City Attorney to join the federal government’s amicus brief challenging
  California’s sanctuary state laws.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:48 p.m., Mayor Sachs declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:03
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

NEW BUSINESS

14.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2017-18

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 18-13 Amending the FY 2017-18 Budget for Adjustments to Certain
  Revenue Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations; (2)
  adopt Resolution 18-14, Amending the City's Salary Schedule and Authorized Position
  Schedule Effective March 27, 2018.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  6  March 27, 2018
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Sachs presented the report.

16. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

17. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

19.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update from Chief Vuong

  Lieutenant Vuong provided an update from Mission Viejo Police Services which included
  case information and an overview of Rapid DNA tests. He also announced upcoming
  commercial enforcement checkpoints, a public safety town hall meeting on April 18, and
  a Special Olympics fundraiser at Claim Jumper restaurant on April 12, 2018.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum encouraged residents to visit the newly redesigned Pavilions grocery
store which, she said, is a great addition to the city and will bring increased revenue. She also
announced that Floor and Décor will be opening at the end of the summer or early fall and is
projected to bring about $250,000 in sales tax revenue each year. New restaurants are also opening
at Crown Valley Parkway and the I-5 freeway and although Toys ‘R Us is closing, Mission Viejo
has a Buy Baby store and Council Member Bucknum encouraged residents to shop there to keep
tax dollars local. She commended Mayor Sachs for his leadership in hosting a Science Technology
Engineering Math (STEM) mentorship program kick-off breakfast. She said it is an amazing
concept to partner businesses with students and the college. Council Member Bucknum also
thanked former Mayor Frank Ury for his presentation on cyber security before the South Orange
City Council Minutes  7  March 27, 2018
 County Economic Coalition. She reminded residents that Bunny Days will be held on Saturday,
March 30 and the grand re-opening of the Marguerite Aquatics Complex will be held Saturday,
April 7. Council Member Bucknum announced that guest will park at Trabuco Hills High School
and take a free shuttle to the event. Attendees cannot park in the neighborhood and shopping
centers adjacent to the aquatics center and should take advantage of the free parking and shuttles.
She said she looks forward to the event and to seeing everyone there.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell sad he attended an enlightening session at the Orange County Council
of Governments General Assembly last week. It was called "Planning a Brighter Future" and
covered topics such as leading in uncertain times, solving homelessness, encouraging cities to
work together, and securing Orange County's water and energy future. He said the latter tied in
very nicely with an agenda item that the Council approved tonight for the timing of traffic signals
and installation of fiber optic cable on Marguerite Parkway. He stated that the improvements will
be a significant asset going forward, particularly as autonomous vehicles start becoming more
commonplace. Council Member Goodell also outlined his attendance at a League of California
Cities meeting that included topics like homelessness, cybersecurity and the sustainability of
California’s retirement system. He noted that there is a lot for the Council to be involved in so they
can protect the course for the citizens and the city in general. In closing, Council Member Goodell
announced that he is looking forward to the grand re-opening of the Marguerite Aquatics Complex
on April 7 and to taking the first swim in the pool. He is also eager to see the great things that will
happen at the facility in the future.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that Assemblyman Brough is working on amendments to the
California Voting Rights Act (CVRA) as AB2231, which will be heard by the legislature on April
25. The bill promotes higher standards for violations of the CVRA and levels the playing field so
that local governments can recover costs along with the plaintiffs. Council Member Kelley said
she would like to see an item on the next agenda to consider supporting that bill as it comes
forward, especially since Mission Viejo has been one of Assemblyman Brough’s motivations for
trying to bring some change to the CVRA. She also discussed her attendance at a Nadadores
Foundation Board Meeting and said it was great to hear how excited they are about the updated
Marguerite Aquatics Complex. The Board Members gave Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay
very nice compliments and shared how much they appreciate him. In addition she attended a
bleeding control training and said it is an excellent course for residents and public sector workers
to take. She will be working with the city staff to promote "stop the bleed kits" to Mission Viejo
schools and she noted that the city already has quite a few kits at its facilities. Bleeding control
training is also available at Mission Hospital on the 4th Wednesday of the month with an additional
training on “National Stop the Bleed Day” which is March 31. Council Member Kelley outlined
her attendance at a ribbon cutting for the new Volvo dealership and Cava restaurant’s food
preview. She drew residents’ attention to Consent Calendar item 10 which was a contract for curb
painting. The city periodically repaints curbs in front of homes and this project will cover the
southern portion of the city and will be completed between April and June this year. Council
Member Kelley commended City Clerk Karen Hamman on the 2017 Annual Report and stated
that it is a creative and informative publication. She encouraged residents to pick up a copy at city
City Council Minutes  8  March 27, 2018
 facilities or look for it online. In conclusion, Council Member Kelley reminded residents of Bunny
Days on March 31 from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center and Earth
Day/Arbor Day on April 21 at Cordova Park.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths joked that anyone watching tonight’s meeting would think that the number
one issue in Mission Viejo is sanctuary cities, but people are really just anxious for Popeyes
Louisiana Kitchen to open. He discussed his attendance last night at a string ensemble performance
by the Orange County Symphony at Montevideo Elementary School and he thanked them for the
invitation. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he sits on the Orange County Veterans Advisory
Council which meets once a month. He shared that since the year 2000, 189 base hospitals have
been shut down causing hundreds of thousands of military personnel to leave California and he
said that will take a toll on the state. Mayor Pro Tem Raths noted that tax revenue is starting to go
down and he's working with the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce on a Buy Local campaign
which he hopes will help with the city's tax income.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs announced that last week at this time he was attending the Laguna Niguel City
Council meeting which dealt with the homeless tent city that the county had ascribed for Laguna
Niguel as one of three locations in the county. He said you don’t put a homeless encampment next
to a library and a preschool and a five minute walk from an elementary school. Mayor Sachs stated
that he was pleased to announce that today, the county Board rescinded its request for three of the
homeless tent city locations including Laguna Niguel. He further noted that while it’s necessary
for cities to be involved in the homeless situation, better locations need to be found. Mayor Sachs
announced that “Secure Orange County Schools” will get started in the next two to three weeks.
This is the group he started along with Undersheriff Don Barnes, local schools and a number of
mayors from South County. The first step is to have each city conduct a meeting with its residents
and stakeholders who can contribute to the conversation. The mayors will then come together share
ideas and start talking about solutions. Mayor Sachs said it’s not always about putting guns in
schools and he’d like to see a School Resource Officer on every campus, including elementary
schools. He noted that there are gaps in security and the goal is to ensure the safety of not only
children, but teachers and administrators in the schools. Mayor Sachs concluded by apologizing
for a comment he made earlier when a public speaker constantly interrupted the meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:11 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, April 10, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.
